sections.title: When and how it changes
sections.text:
- After every owner message, every answer we give and every change to the system, always last, once the other docs are updated.
- The agent saves the message first, finds the sections it touches and rewrites those passages, so the README still reads as one story about today.
- "Where things stand", "What comes next" and "Open questions" are checked every time: an answered question leaves the list, and something built stops being called planned.
- If the one-paragraph description of the project changes, the short front page of the repo is brought in line too.

- The knowledge base agent reads it before writing any other doc, so facts and words stay the same everywhere.

n-2.5.text: What is built now, next and later, so agents work on the right thing. The current phase is planning: nothing is built, and the owner reviews the design object by object. n-2.6.text: The decision log: an append-only history of what the owner decided, when, why and from which input, so settled questions are not reopened. Each entry has an id, date, decision, reasons, sources and a status (active, partly superseded, superseded); the rule itself lives in a topic doc that points back here. The knowledge agent records owner decisions while processing an input. Self-improvement and support agents may add proposals marked "pending owner", which the owner approves or rejects in the UI.
keep: When you record a decision, write the rule in the topic doc that owns it; this log only says when and why.
When you propose a change to a shared file or the common prompt, add it here marked "pending owner" and wait for the owner.
When a decision is replaced, mark the old entry superseded instead of editing or deleting it.

n-2.7.text: The rules that keep hundreds of agents consistent and machine-readable: agent names (unique ids, variant formats, no renames), the `.link` rule and file links, script kinds, per-agent configs, the standard agent and `.claude/` folders, tests and research, content folders and child links, the links file, where a new file goes, docs and git. n-2.8.text: The rules no agent may break, about money, keys and approvals. It covers test and live for every action, live money approved only by the owner in the UI, every new strategy configuration approved by the owner before it starts, hard risk limits in code, secrets kept in `.secrets/` and loaded by key name at run time, external text as untrusted (protection layers come with live trading), and the kill switch. The system's SI sub-agent reads errors and costs here. The events are proposed; file naming and retention are open.
keep: When you log a key event, write key names, mode and result only; never a value.

n-15.2.text: One log folder per acting service, named after it, such as `polymarket-exec`. Every action, test or live, is one JSONL line: who acted, mode, account, the order and its result (`simulated_fill`, `filled`, `rejected`, `blocked_by_risk`, `blocked_by_kill_switch`). These lines are the source of every PnL, win-rate and drawdown number, and positions are rebuilt from them until they get a home. The format is proposed; how an agent reads only its own lines is open.
keep: When you build an acting service, log every action here, test or live, blocked ones included.

n-15.3.text: One log folder per shared worker, named after it. The draft format is plain text: a dated `YYYY-MM-DD.log` plus a stable `latest.log`, one line per event (`ts LEVEL worker message`). At the end of each run the worker also prints a JSON summary line that `run-job` keeps in the job log. An agent links `latest.log` only when it needs it. Whether these logs become JSONL like the others is open.
keep: When you rotate dated logs, keep replacing `latest.log` in one step; agents' links point at it.

n-15.4.text: One log folder per system sub-agent, named after it, such as `news-digest`. Each call is one JSONL line: time, sub-agent, model, number of input files, output path, duration, cost and status. The cost of a shared sub-agent counts to the level that runs it, not to its readers (still open). The format is proposed.
keep: When you log a call's cost, name the field `cost_usd`; the drafts' `usd` does not match the other logs.

n-15.text: The system's shared logs, sorted by source, and the UI's starting point for every log in the system. `system/` holds the machinery's JSONL log (scheduler, triggers, relink and link checks, loaded or refused keys, errors, costs); `services/` holds one line per test or live action, the source of all PnL; `workers/` holds the shared workers' logs; `subagents/` one line per sub-agent call with its cost. The system-level agent and the home of everything shared. Like every level it has the standard agent folder, and its agent manages all domains, system health and the development of the system itself, and answers the owner's questions about the whole system.

What makes it different: its content folders also hold the shared files every agent uses. `configs/` has the global config and model routing, `scripts/` the shared machinery (create-agent, the one scheduler, relink, load-secret, run-tests, build-map), `logs/` and `data/` the shared logs and worker outputs, and `docs/` the knowledge base of the whole OS. Its `.claude/` holds the system prompt and the system-wide sub-agents, among them the knowledge agent that keeps the docs and these summaries current.

Agents use shared files through read-only file links, never copies; anything needed by only one agent stays in that agent's folder. The system reaches each domain through `subagents.link/`, and strategies and variants one level further down each time. `init.sh` installs the git hooks and relinks the project; `start.sh` starts the scheduler and the system session (proposed).
keep: When a second agent needs something agent-local, move it into the matching shared folder here and give both a file link (proposed).
When an owner input or a system change comes in, run it through the knowledge agent so the docs and summaries stay current.

All agents of the Trading OS, one folder per domain. The system is a domain too: `system/` holds the system agent and everything shared, `prediction-market-agents/` is the first trading domain, and `copy-trading-agents/` comes next. Inside a trading domain sit its strategy agents, and inside each strategy its trading variants.

Every level (system, domain, strategy, variant) uses one identical agent folder: `.claude/` with the level's prompt, then `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `research/` and the level files. Each content folder holds the level's own files, file links to what it reads elsewhere, and `subagents.link/` to its children. Agents are created by `create-agent`; domain and strategy self-improvement create new variants. Secrets, the UI and cloned apps live outside this folder.
keep: When you add an agent, give it a unique name and the standard folder through `create-agent`; never copy a folder by hand.
When an agent needs another agent's file, add a link to its links file; it never writes into another agent's folder.

n-0.text:
The Trading OS workspace: an agentic trading system that runs many trading agents side by side, tests every idea in test mode first, compares the results and keeps what works, with the owner approving every new strategy variant and anything that touches real money.

Workers collect data on schedules, sub-agents pre-analyse it, and agents at four levels (system, domain, strategy, trading variant) decide and improve themselves, each in the same standard folder. Every agent's jobs, links and config are plain files the owner can open and edit, and data is JSON and Markdown.

At the root: `agents/` (every agent, the system's shared files and the knowledge base in `agents/system/docs/`), `.secrets/` (keys, outside `agents/`, git-ignored), `trading-ui/` (the owner's view and controls), `apps/` (cloned repos), `README.md` and `.gitignore`.

The knowledge agent keeps the docs and every How it works summary current after each owner input or change. Nothing is built yet; much of the design is proposed. It will run on one of the owner's servers and must move easily to a bigger one. Still open: one repo or several. The full "Always keep in mind" list is in `overview.md`.
keep: When anything needs a secret, list the key name in `secret_keys` and let `load-secret` load it; never write a value anywhere.
When you add or change a link, edit the agent's links file and let `relink` build it; never make a symlink by hand.
When you change an agent's config, prompt, code or model, make a new test variant; only the owner approves live money.
When the owner says something about the system, or you change it, run it through the knowledge agent.
